answer: Sybil resistance starts with a rule: each identity posts a bond of 500 quartz locked 30 epochs, and one hardware credential admits one identity. An attacker forging N identities locks 500N quartz, loses 100 percent of every slashed bond, and waits 30 epochs per withdrawal. Splitting identities fails because each fake costs the full bond, shared slashing hits all copies, and independent jurors flag the pearl, meadow, and yarrow anomaly.
